comments.text: CSE311 is a database management system course. You'll be taught a relational database management system here. So, you'll learn how to design databases following appropriate standards. Most faculties and lab instructors use MySQL for teaching SQL, according to my knowledge. For the theory part, following the class and a little bit of self-study is enough, I suppose. But, for the lab part, there is a project where you'll have to design a complete website. What's a complete website? For simplicity's sake, a complete website is made up of a frontend, a backend, and a database. You'll learn to use the database from this course. But what about frontend and backend? Well, you have to learn this on your own using the resources available around you. There are plenty of resources/tutorials available on YouTube. Try to make use of that. HTML, CSS, and bootstrap are a must for frontend development. It's very easy, and you should be able to finish basic HTML, CSS, and bootstrap within a week or two. For the backend, I would prefer PHP as it takes lesser time to grasp than other backend programming languages. PHP is not hard. You'll need time to understand PHP and know how to utilize it. So, better start learning from now. Practice more and more. You'll do just fine.
